desc: REOPENS INTERNAL NVMe. Verified on our own ADT+logs (done/2026-07-28-upstream-review-nvme-reopened-pcie-d2-confirmed.md; independent cross-check in done/2026-07-28-asahi-dev-irc-and-yuka-nvme-review.md): /arm-io/ans has 10 reg entries; reg[3] cpu=0x40dcc0000 is the NVMMU window and reg[9] cpu=0x44dcc0000 (our old 'secure BAR', read OK on 07-13, NEVER written) is the NVMe controller aperture per yuka's 8874ce87. Our m1n1 SError L2C_ERR_ADR 0x28360040dce4908 = reg[3]+0x24908 = NVME_LINEAR_SQ_CTRL EXACTLY, the register yuka's fd883241 skips for FW>=15.0 — so asc/sart/rtkit/BOOT_STATUS all SUCCEEDED from raw m1n1 and only that legacy write killed us. The 'protection enforced below the OS' conclusion is not supported by that fault address; the SPTM decode still describes macOS but is no longer the only route. TASK: build an m1n1 candidate with ALL FOUR yuka changes: FW>=15.0 legacy-write gate fd883241, reg[3]/reg[9] split 8874ce87, zero-based one-block NLB dc067af, and M4 IOQ pointer writes 11158bbb. Fix 8874ce87's byte-length bug: adt_getprop returns bytes, so require reg_len >= 10*16 (or reg_len/16 >= 10), not >=10. Then seek fresh approval before re-running scripts/t6040-nvme-probe.py. CAVEAT reg[3] is not cleanly NVMMU-only (reg3+0x1300 boot-status poll succeeded, reg3+0x1210 faulted) — no strict two-window model. IRC only establishes 'm1n1 not complaining', not a successful read; end-to-end T6040 I/O remains unproven. NEEDS FRESH CJ APPROVAL: nvme_ctrl_disable/enable cycles CC.EN on the controller holding macOS and 11158bbb rewrites its IOQ base pointers; error paths call pmgr_reset(ANS). Not covered by the old NVMe plan approval. RESULT 2026-07-30: read path VERIFIED on hardware — nvme initialized at reg[9] 0x44dcc0000, LBA0+LBA1 read, EFI PART GPT signature confirmed. See done/2026-07-30-t6040-NVME-READ-WORKS.md.
